# Top of the list

Class A repositories that a second pass over the rubric confirmed. Unaudited rows are not here, however high they scored.

There are two doors into class A: a total of 11 or more, or relevance 3 together with novelty 2 or more. The second door is a wide one — it lets in a repository whose idea transfers even when little else about it does — so the rows that also carry a high total are kept in a section of their own.

### Command line tools

- [shiftynick/jev-axi](https://github.com/shiftynick/jev-axi) — 12/15 — D3 R3 N2 M2 E2 — An agent-ergonomic CLI for Jev: pick/rate/check/ask/rank/filter/find/diff/files/triage/guard/progress/commit commands, a PreToolUse security hook, band policy \(act/confirm/escalate\) — A mature reference CLI mapping almost one-to-one to an agent harness \(route/triage/gate/check/skill/ask/stats/feedback/eval\): \(1\) a 'band' policy \(act&gt;=0.75/confirm&gt;=0.45/escalate below\) with adjustable thresholds; \(2\) a separate yes/no 'match_exists' question accompanying ranking questions, ensuring an empty result is a definite judgment rather than 'least-bad option'; \(3\) a 'progress' command checking whether work is ACTUALLY done \(exit 3 until finished\) — the direct CLI counterpart of the 'tests passed is a claim, not evidence' principle; \(4\) triage saying 'no error' instead of FABRICATING a root cause when there is none; \(5\) a VERY valuable honest negative finding: they couldn't show their own 'file ranking' feature provided real benefit in their own benchmarks AND the agent skill never loaded it on its own — publishing this without hiding it in the main README is exemplary honesty; \(6\) resolving routine commands locally/at zero cost and only sending risky ones to Jev, redacting credentials before sending — A near one-to-one counterpart to a typical agent-harness setup \(CLI + PreToolUse hook + act/confirm/escalate band\); the benchmark is honest enough to show both a 25% gain and a 29% loss. — [evidence](https://github.com/shiftynick/jev-axi#readme)

### Code review hooks

### Evaluation and benchmarks

- [aaravriyer193/OpenSmoke](https://github.com/aaravriyer193/OpenSmoke) — 12/15 — D3 R3 N2 M2 E2 — Captures 'silently failed' states in agent traces with four states \(silent/disclosed/recovered/clean\); scans first with cheap questions and escalates only flagged ones to an LLM for root cause; openly acknowledges its own model's \(Jev\) published weak hit rate \(68%\) — A two-stage architecture capturing 'the environment broke but it wasn't disclosed to the user' with a silent/disclosed/recovered/clean taxonomy, scanning first with cheap typed questions and escalating only flagged ones to a strong LLM for root cause, plus clustering runs with the same root cause into a SINGLE event, plus the honesty of openly acknowledging its own model's published weak hit rate as the reason for adding a second opinion; directly applicable as a tool wholesale-auditing 'completed' claims across agent runs — Captures 'the environment broke and the agent silently worked around it' via silent/disclosed/recovered/clean states; openly states its own model's 68% agreement rate. — [evidence](https://github.com/aaravriyer193/OpenSmoke#readme)
- [Adilmp/does-jev-confidence-mean-anything](https://github.com/Adilmp/does-jev-confidence-mean-anything) — 12/15 — D1 R3 N3 M2 E3 — A calibration study auditing whether Jev's confidence scores are meaningful, using 8,000 human-labeled judgments at $0.05 cost — A calibration-audit methodology recalibrating on half the data and measuring on the other half \(ECE/AUC, reliability diagram\); directly applicable to testing two providers' 'confidence' claims before trusting them — A calibration audit with 8,000 human labels: where 75% confidence is reported, the real rate is 10%. Ranking is good, absolute thresholds aren't; a two-parameter correction removes 96% of the error. — [evidence](https://github.com/Adilmp/does-jev-confidence-mean-anything#readme)
- [amr05008/jev-sandbox](https://github.com/amr05008/jev-sandbox) — 12/15 — D2 R3 N2 M2 E3 — An experiment set testing when Jev can be used instead of an LLM: email-triage and gluten-detection comparisons — An experiment template \(a RESULTS.md per experiment\) measuring the Jev-vs-LLM decision with real data \(agreement/speed/cost\) is directly applicable to eval/stats module; confidence-threshold and reference-label audit patterns are also reusable — An experiment template that measures the Jev-vs-LLM question with a 996-item labeled comparison; directly relevant to eval/stats. — [evidence](https://github.com/amr05008/jev-sandbox#readme)
- [clduab11/jev-test](https://github.com/clduab11/jev-test) — 12/15 — D3 R3 N2 M2 E2 — A pre-registered pilot experiment leaving all decisions \(search/evidence/sufficiency/verification\) to Jev so a small local model can answer web questions without hallucination — Splitting the RAG/search pipeline into a sequence of small typed Jev decisions instead of one large model \(is search needed, does this count as evidence, is it sufficient, is every sentence supported\); zero wrong answers in the pilot, an architecture applicable to search-verification flow — A pre-registered pilot that hands all of a small local model's decisions \(search/evidence/sufficiency/sentence support\) to Jev; 'declining to answer' is a first-class outcome. — [evidence](https://github.com/clduab11/jev-test)

### Security and prompt injection

- [leepokai/jev-guard](https://github.com/leepokai/jev-guard) — 11/15 — D3 R3 N2 M2 E1 — A security hook running across 8 different coding-agent/hosts; makes a deny/ask/allow decision with four typed questions \(risk/approval/user_requested/from_untrusted\), scans instruction files \(skill/CLAUDE.md\) for leakage/hidden execution — An explicit decision tree with four typed questions: from_untrusted always triggers deny, user_requested can flip ask to allow but never removes deny. Scanning 'instruction files' like Skill/CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md at install/load time for exfiltration/hidden-execution/canaries \(measured false-positive rate across 662 real skills\) — the most mature direct example for security-injection/freeze-gate design — A security hook across eight agent hosts; from_untrusted always denies, user_requested can turn ask into allow but never lift a deny. Also scans instruction files. — [evidence](https://github.com/leepokai/jev-guard)

### Text generation experiments

- [rhighs/jev-code](https://github.com/rhighs/jev-code) — 10/15 — D3 R3 N2 M2 E0 — The LLM suggests semantic sub-problems/code options, Jev approves/selects/reviews; the LLM can never approve a plan, choose a tool, or write a file — Against skibidu's finding that Jev ALONE building code node-by-node failed, here the LLM SUGGESTS sub-problems/code options but has no authority to approve the plan/select a tool/write a file — only Jev approves. This hybrid separation preserves the LLM's generative power while removing decision authority — direct evidence for an 'LLM suggests, a narrow typed model approves' model in an agent tool-call architecture. The idea of turning a Jev decision into an independent CLI primitive \(stdin-&gt;exit code\) like `jev-code decide` could inspire a general 'decide' command addable to an agent harness CLI — The LLM suggests sub-problems/options, but can't approve the plan, pick tools, or write files; policy lives only in Jev.
